subsystems.name: Primary mirror (M1)
parts: 798 hexagonal segments, each 1.4 m across and about 5 cm thick
segment support cell with position actuators
edge sensors that measure misalignment between neighbours

subsystems.name: Adaptive optics relay
subsystems.role: corrects atmospheric turbulence hundreds of times per second.
parts: M4, a thin deformable mirror with thousands of actuators
M5, a fast tip-tilt mirror that stabilises the beam
wavefront sensors and laser guide stars

subsystems.name: Structure and enclosure
subsystems.role: holds the optics in alignment while the telescope tracks the sky.

subsystems.name: High-contrast imaging
subsystems.role: suppresses the glare of the star so a faint planet can be seen beside it.

subsystems.name: Science instruments
subsystems.role: split the light into spectra at the Nasmyth foci.

subsystems.name: Site infrastructure
subsystems.role: supplies the stable conditions the optics need.
parts: summit platform on Cerro Armazones, Chile
mirror coating and segment storage facilities

buildSteps.title: Prepare the summit
buildSteps.detail: The top of Cerro Armazones in Chile's Atacama Desert was blasted and levelled to create a stable platform and a road up to it.

buildSteps.title: Make the mirror segments
buildSteps.detail: 798 hexagonal blanks are cast from a low-expansion glass-ceramic, then ground and polished to a surface accurate to a few tens of nanometres.

buildSteps.title: Build the dome and foundation
buildSteps.detail: A concrete pier is poured to carry the telescope, and the steel dome is erected around it.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the mount
buildSteps.detail: The altitude and azimuth structures are fitted on hydrostatic bearings and the drives and encoders installed.

buildSteps.title: Install M1
buildSteps.detail: Each segment is lifted into the mirror cell, attached to its support with actuators and edge sensors, and roughly positioned.

buildSteps.title: Fit the adaptive optics relay
buildSteps.detail: M4 and M5 plus the optical relay are installed on their optical path and cabled to the real-time control system.

buildSteps.title: Mount the instruments
buildSteps.detail: First-generation spectrographs and imagers are installed at the Nasmyth foci and cooled to operating temperature.

buildSteps.title: Cophase and align
buildSteps.detail: The segments are driven to act as one continuous mirror — a tolerance far finer than a human hair — and the adaptive system is tuned.

buildSteps.title: Commission and verify
buildSteps.detail: Laser guide stars, coronagraphy and instrument modes are tested on real targets before science operations begin.

prerequisites.why: proven by the 10-metre Keck telescopes; without it a 39-metre monolithic mirror cannot be made or transported.
thousands of actuators moving a thin mirror in step are what cancel atmospheric blur.
a bright artificial star lets the correction work where the sky has no natural reference star.
edge sensors and fast computers keep 798 segments phased as the telescope moves.
starlight suppression at this contrast has been shown on smaller telescopes but must be scaled up.
they resolve the narrow spectral lines that separate a planet's light from its star's.

pathway.milestone: construction at Cerro Armazones; segments polished, tested and stored, structure and dome assembled
pathway.unlocks: the machine exists and can begin integration.

pathway.milestone: first light, expected in the late 2020s, with the first instruments at the Nasmyth foci
pathway.unlocks: observations of the early Universe and of planets around other stars at a new level of detail.

pathway.milestone: commissioning of extreme adaptive optics and coronagraphy
pathway.unlocks: direct images and spectra of gas-giant exoplanets orbiting nearby stars.

pathway.milestone: combining the telescope with interferometric facilities and upgraded instruments
pathway.unlocks: higher resolution, characterisation of smaller planets and studies of their atmospheres.
